Most people think creativity is a gift. It's not. It's a skill, and AI is about to make it the most important one you have.

This episode is about the paradox at the center of every creative tool you're using right now. AI can make you more prolific than ever, but used without judgment, it can also make you invisible faster than anything else. I call it synthetic sameness, and it's already everywhere.

I've spent my career moving between mathematics, music, business, and AI, and the clearest lesson I've drawn from all of it is this: your originality and your taste are the two things no model can generate for you.

So in this video, I'll walk you through the EDGE framework, four principles for creating with AI without losing your edge.

You'll learn how to:

- Hold your work to a higher standard when AI will never run out of mediocre versions
- Move away from AI defaults and bring a point of view that actually stands out
- Ground everything you create in verifiable reality, not confident hallucination
- Make your work feel something, because that part still has to come from you

Along the way, I'll walk through Christopher Nolan flipping a real truck on LaSalle Street, a 95-minute AI film that generated 16,000 clips to find 253, a startup that made a $2,000 ad that reached 18 million people during the NBA Finals, and the AI band that hit Spotify's viral chart without a single human in the room.

AI can paint the candle flame. Only you can make it mean something.

Thank you, and I love you.
